summary: High-level planning for a joint marketplace listing and reference architecture targeting GalaxyEdge's edge-aware multi-cloud platform. Discussed packaging options, security/compliance gating, deploy patterns (VPC peering vs private link), and an initial pilot on dedicated capacity. Agreed on artifacts and timeline for pilot readiness.
topics: Marketplace listing requirements and approval path
Reference architecture: edge cluster patterns and routing
Packaging: container image + helm chart vs operator
Security: KMS, audit logs, SOC2/iso concerns
Pilot plan: metrics, perf benchmarks, rollback/fallback policies
transcript:
00:00 Lena (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, we got a pretty full agenda for 45 ish minutes, quick intros?
00:12 Priya (GalaxyEdge): hi, Priya here, CTO, happy to dig in — we've got folks from platform and cloud arch.
00:18 Ethan (GalaxyEdge): Ethan, platform eng, we'll own the infra side.
00:22 Marco (Redwood SE): Marco here, i run integrations for marketplace and ref archs. apologies for slightly delayed wifi earlier.
00:30 Sofia (GalaxyEdge): Sofia - cloud architect, focused on multi-cloud glue and networking.
00:40 Lena: cool, objective is to map out the listing requirements and the ref-arch patterns we want to ship with, and identify any blockers around security or data residency.
01:05 Priya: quick context — GalaxyEdge runs customer workloads at edge PoPs and on major clouds, we care about small model footprints, cold-starts, and also storefront listing so our customers can discover the joint offering.
01:30 Marco: makes sense — couple clarifying qs: do you expect us to provide an operator/helm, or is a simple container + docs enough to list?
01:42 Sofia: we prefer operator for lifecycle (heal, scale), but we can accept helm if we get hooks for KV cache persistence and for metrics. Operator adds more approval steps on our side though.
02:05 Lena: noted. The marketplace team will want a reproducible install path; operator is fine but if it's heavier we should agree on a phased approach: 1) helm chart listing, 2) operator in a later patch.
02:30 Ethan: talk to us about network topologies — we have customers that require VPC peering and others that want private endpoint (private link). Which does Redwood support in private deployments?
02:48 Marco: Redwood Private supports VPC peering, PrivateLink-style endpoints, and air-gapped installs. There are a couple of differences: peering keeps routing simple but requires route table config, private endpoint is cleaner for tenant isolation. Also, we do KMS integration for model keys.
03:12 Priya: KMS — we need to ensure our HSM vendor is supported. We use Vault backed by an HSM in some regions. Is that okay?
03:22 Marco: yes, our Private control plane can integrate with customer KMS via standard APIs; we have a vault connector in our reference arch. We'll include a sample config.
04:15 Jonas (GalaxyEdge): any blockers around certification or compliance? we have customers in finance and healthcare.
04:25 Lena: we'll surface SOC2 and ISO artifacts and audit log capabilities. For healthcare/PHI you'll want on-prem or VPC private deployments; we'll call out that listing may require additional attestation.
05:00 Marco: perf question — do you have target latency for model calls at the edge?
05:08 Priya: target p95 under 100ms for small gen and embeddings for local tenant, but we can accept slightly higher for cross-region.
05:20 Marco: ok that's helpful — we'll propose a batching/cache config that keeps p95 near that. note there are trade-offs between quantization and quality as well.
06:00 Sofia: what about image sizes and container footprint? we try to limit images to under 2GB for fast pull — do you provide quantized model bundles?
06:12 Marco: yes, we can publish quantized variants (4-bit, 8-bit). For marketplace listing we can include a default quantized build and a full-precision optional build. we'll add image size estimates in the ref arch doc.
07:05 Priya: onboarding flow for customers via the marketplace — once they click 'deploy' we need a manifest to spin up our infra and set permissions. Is there a standard manifest you expect?
07:20 Lena: we have a listing manifest template — it'll require fields for roles, endpoints, required secrets, and a health-check endpoint. i'll send the template after the call.
07:40 Ethan: on perf testing — can we run a short benchmark? a dedicated window to hammer requests and validate cold starts?
07:50 Marco: yes, pilot plan could be a 2-week dedicated capacity run with perf suite. we'll need access to a test cluster and representative requests.
08:10 Priya: ok we'll assemble a sample dataset and give test creds.
08:22 Marco: noted - also, for fallback, we recommend a multi-variant route: if edge capacity is constrained, route to a nearby region-hosted variant. That should be in the failover policy.
09:05 Sofia: about telemetry — we need traces and token-level cost metrics surfaced for our tenant customers. do you expose Prometheus metrics and tracing?
09:20 Marco: yes we expose prometheus endpoints, and we can hook tracing via OTEL. The marketplace listing will call out required scraping endpoints and RBAC rules.
09:40 Lena: sounds like we have three buckets of deliverables: (A) marketplace checklist and manifest template, (B) ref-arch doc with operator/helm patterns + network topologies, (C) pilot run plan with perf benchmarks and dataset. We'll assign owners.
10:10 Priya: question on billing — how does metering work if we do listing through GalaxyEdge's marketplace? do you support SSO billing handoff?
10:30 Lena: two main patterns: direct billing to Redwood, or reseller/marketplace billing where you bill customers and we invoice GalaxyEdge. we'll share pricing bands. SSO for admin is fine; billing handoff will require contract work.
11:05 Jonas: any competitors in this space we should be mindful of?
11:12 Marco: CloudVendorX has a similar marketplace plugin but they are less optimized for small edge footprints, EdgeServe focuses on edge orchestration but lacks integrated inference batching. we should highlight that in the joint value props.
12:00 Ethan: security deep-dive later? we might need a follow-up with our compliance lead for SOC2 details.
12:10 Lena: yes let's schedule a security review call; Marco can join for technical gating.
12:30 Priya: timeline — we want marketplace listing in Q3, pilot in June end to July. is that feasible?
12:42 Marco: conservative plan: produce artifacts by 6/9, internal review 6/11, pilot config and infra ready by 6/22, pilot window last week of June.
13:05 Lena: ok recap — deliverables noted. i'll share the listing checklist and Marco will deliver the ref-arch one-pager. Priya/Ethan will share manifests and sample dataset.
13:25 Priya: thanks, that helps. any open risks?
13:32 Marco: main risk is KMS/region parity and operator approval on GalaxyEdge's side; we'll try helm-first to speed listing.
13:50 Sofia: also image size/cold-starts — we might ask for model pruning recommendations if needed.
14:05 Lena: good — action items on the sheet. We'll put the next sync on the calendar for 2026-06-16 to review artifacts.
14:20 Ethan: noted. thanks all.
14:30 Meeting closed.
